title: Static Electricity
standard_code: Grade 5, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy
standard_text: Objects become charged by rubbing; like charges repel and unlike charges attract; static electricity is seen in daily life, including lightning. (summary of the MATATAG Science curriculum, Grade 5, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy)
meta_desc: Free Grade 5 Science worksheets (MATATAG, Quarter 3: Force, Motion, and Energy): electric charges, attract and repel, static in daily life, electricity and magnetism and charge investigations. 100 questions with answers.
key_big: Like charges repel; unlike charges attract.
key_sub: Rubbing moves electrons, so objects build up static charge until it jumps as a spark.
body_html:
How to think about it

Static electricity is electric charge that builds up on the surface of an object.

  • Rubbing two materials moves electrons from one to the other.
  • Like charges (+ and +, or − and −) repel. Unlike charges (+ and −) attract.
  • A spark or shock happens when built-up charge jumps. Lightning is a giant spark.
Example

Two balloons both rubbed on hair are held close. What happens?

both have the same charge

Answer: they repel

Example

Why does a comb rubbed on dry hair pick up bits of paper?

charged objects attract neutral ones

Answer: the charged comb attracts the paper

Common mistakes

  • Thinking static electricity flows in a circuit.
  • Thinking charged objects are magnets.
  • Thinking protons move when objects are rubbed.

faq.a: Rubbing moves electrons from one material to another, so one becomes negative and the other positive.

faq.q: Why does a balloon stick to a wall?
faq.a: The charged balloon pulls opposite charges in the wall closer, so they attract.

faq.q: How can you stay safe in a thunderstorm?
faq.a: Go indoors, stay away from tall trees, water and metal fences, and wait 30 minutes after the last thunder.

items.q: In Joy's test, a comb has a positive charge and a bit of paper has a negative charge. They are held close but not touching. What happens?
c: Nothing happens; they must touch first.
They attract only if they touch.
items.e: Like charges repel; opposite charges attract, even without touching.

items.q: Thunder is heard after lightning is seen. Why?

items.e: The rubbed balloon has a static electric charge that attracts the hair.
